paper_findings: The Euler–Lagrange system as printed (l.386–387) is inconsistent under l.249's convention (−Δ + V, Δ = div∇): with the outward normal the divergence theorem forces μ = 0, while μ = 2 cap* > 0; the inward normal describes −v, and the pairing claim at l.405–406 holds only with Δ = −div∇. The correct system is −Δv = μ/(2V) in Σ with the printed boundary condition (argued; only the weak form is in Lean, Yamabe.euler_lagrange).

statements.blocked_on: OQ-109 (the correction of record); 0 < λ₁ and a finite C_SP are proved on the C¹ reading (Mfd.readingModel_thm_star3_corrected)
paper_findings: The proof is wrong (l.635, l.645–647; proved against the paper): « G is non-decreasing » fails, since the cap n₆ = min{C_SP X₀, 2} makes G decrease past 2/C_SP (Yamabe.star3G_not_monotone: G(4) < G(2) at V = λ₁ = C_SP = 1), and case (ii) uses G(X) ≤ G(X₀), which fails e.g. at X = 2/C_SP.

The printed Ã (l.607–611) is not a valid constant on the model of record: a two-point model (masses 1/100, 99/100, V = 1) meets every hypothesis and u = (1, 1/5) needs Ã ≥ 0.27 against ≤ 0.22 printed (thm_star3_printed_false). The model violates lem:csp-lower (C_SP = 0.4595 < 0.538), so against a Riemannian Σ this is argued, not proved: a dumbbell with a neck of conductance κ → 0, every constant scaling like 1/κ, gives 0.211 against 0.270.

The table at l.660 (λ₁V^{2/3} = 4π², V = 1): the corrected minima are 1.070, 1.509, 2.508, 4.682 and the printed formula's own minima 0.375, 0.490, 1.000, 2.250 at C_SP = 0.539, 0.70, 1.0, 1.5, against 1.073, 1.511, 1.915, 2.250 printed; the first two agree with the corrected minimum, 2.250 only with the printed formula, 1.915 with neither (numerical, not formalized).

statements.label: thm:upper
statements.scope_notes: T-perf-upper (atlas-team, 2026-11-23), audit AUDIT-1 minor (the ρ wording, a SCOPE bullet; fixed). MARKED in Yamabe/Perforated/Upper.lean, sorry-free: thm_upper as printed for every competitor ψ (the paper's minimiser is one), with thm_upper_strong (no ρ factor, no proviso) and thm_upper_capD (cap_D an inf in [0, ∞]); cap* ≤ cap_D, θ ≤ θ_D.
statements.notes: T-perf-upper (atlas-team, 2026-11-23), audit AUDIT-1 minor (the ρ wording, a SCOPE bullet; fixed). MARKED in Yamabe/Perforated/Upper.lean, sorry-free: thm_upper as printed for every competitor ψ (the paper's minimiser is one), with thm_upper_strong (no ρ factor, no proviso) and thm_upper_capD (cap_D an inf in [0, ∞]); cap* ≤ cap_D, θ ≤ θ_D.
paper_findings: thm:upper (l.871–889) is true as printed but lossy: since ∫ψ = 0, ∫u_s = V for every s, so Hölder against 1 gives ‖u_s‖_{p*} ≥ V^{1/p*}, replacing the triangle-inequality step at l.885; hence λ_∂ ≤ θ_D/(1+θ_D)·F_g(1), with no (1−ρ)^{-2} and no proviso ρ < 1 (Lean Yamabe.thm_upper_strong). The proviso ρ < 1 does not follow from the model's axioms (ρ = 1 on the two-point toy model); on the Euclidean 3-ball ρ ≈ 0.874 (the auditor's numerical integration). Consequences: eq:sandwich's right side becomes θ_D/(1+θ_D), and thm:sharp needs only θ_D/θ → 1, not ρ → 0.
Minor (l.862–866): cap_D is defined through a minimiser whose existence the paper does not prove; the Lean statements do not need it (thm_upper for every competitor, thm_upper_capD with the infimum).

statements.label: cor:yamabe
statements.scope_notes: T-perf-cor-yamabe (atlas-team, 2026-11-23), audit AUDIT-1 clean: Yamabe/Perforated/CorYamabe.lean, strict, sorry-free. Partial, unmarked. Stated without proof in the paper (l.929–939); its content is yamabe's thm:lower-bound, so it is restated over Yamabe/LowerBound.lean (nothing re-proved: cor_yamabe_of_eq_main calls the strict lower_bound_of_eq_main and upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos). Six anchors, one per form of thm:lower-bound (both forms of thm:main, the proved Ã at N = 3 and N ≥ 3, the manifold reading under OQ-93); each takes its counterpart's hypotheses with Yb(Σ) = 0 carried (hYb) in place of σ^∂ ≥ 0. Conclusions: R_g ≡ c < 0 and Y = c·Vol^{2/N}; eq:yamabe-upper Y ≤ −λ_∂ (proved); δ = Yb + ∣R_g∣Vol^{2/N} ≥ Yb + λ_∂ for every Yb, so ∣R_g∣Vol^{2/N} = δ at Yb = 0; θ/(1+θ)F_g(1)(1 + corRem) positive and ≤ λ_∂ ≤ δ, with 1 + corRem exactly thm:main's ((1+θ)/θ)/Λ_max; the M form for round B_j; corRem = O(F) uniformly in θ. « The constant is 1/2 » as an implication (corConst_tendsto_half). Broader than printed: Σ̄ need not be a torus. Non-vacuity: Yamabe.toy_cor_yamabe.

statements.blocked_on: OQ-125 (Yb(Σ) = 0; M; the θ clause; the O(F) factor), OQ-121 (c), OQ-93, OQ-111; the θ → 1 clause on T-perf-dilute-limit (needs-ruling)
paper_findings: Yb(Σ) = 0 (l.925–926), used for « = δ » (l.934), is asserted and proved in neither paper: yamabe's eq:sigma-torus covers T³ only, as an argument that bounds Y_[g] from above, not below; nothing for N ≥ 4. The bound on ∣R_g∣Vol^{2/N} itself needs no Yb.

M (l.931–932) is never defined in the companion (the letter names a manifold, l.287–288, and the 2×2 matrix, l.529–543); for a non-round B_j at N = 3 Minkowski's inequality makes F_g(1) < 2(N−1)M/Vol^{(N−2)/N}, so the M form does not follow from the argument (argued).

Minor (l.938): θ → 1 is prop:theta-examples (ii)'s, at N = 3, in the dilute limit, for the scalar-flat collar; the corollary's g has constant negative scalar curvature and θ is not conformally invariant.
Remark: the inequality holds for every Σ̄ with σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0, and « δ ≥ λ_∂ whenever Yb ≥ 0 » holds in the sharper form δ = Yb + ∣R_g∣Vol^{2/N} ≥ Yb + λ_∂; the O(F_g(1)) is uniform in θ.
